event.label: Still listed in 1940, the last directory transcribed so far

body.p: Leicester Place is a lane off the east side of Leicester Street, between Queensberry and Pelham streets, beside the Carlton Inn (today the Corkman Hotel).
It is first listed in the directories in 1873. It is missing from the 1874 to 1878 directories, and then listed in every directory from 1879 to 1940, the last one transcribed so far.

div.head: Along the street
div.p: In the Leicester Street listings the turn into Leicester Place comes just before the Carlton Inn and its stables. From 1900 the directory gives its corner with Leicester Street as its only crossing.

div.head: Businesses and landmarks

list.item: The Carlton Inn stables, listed in Leicester Place in 1890.
The Hi-Rev Bearing and Engineering Co., motor bearing manufacturers, and a garage of the Economic Cash Buying Co. Pty Ltd (1940).

div.p: In 1930 and 1935 one house is listed only as "Greeks".
